mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate improving consumer confidence and construction activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic expansion accelerates.
failure_condition: HOUST rises above 850 but 20-day SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.15% signals aggressive monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.15% in the past 12 months but 20-day SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and employment (PAYEMS) signal robust manufacturing and labor market conditions, driving positive equity returns over the next 20 days through stronger corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: INDPRO and PAYEMS both exceed thresholds but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 7.5%), a declining unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings expectations for positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 7.5% but 20-day SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates accelerating manufacturing output, which typically generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate demand for capital goods.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises above 98.0 but 5-day SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPIAUCSL exceeding 2.5% signals inflationary pressure, prompting expectations of central bank tightening that reduces equity valuations and generates negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL yoy > 2.5% but 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days through elevated consumption and business investment.
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST both exceed thresholds but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: In low-unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 5.0), rising employment levels (PAYEMS > 135000) signal labor market tightening, which typically generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days through accelerated wage growth and consumer spending.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 5.0 and PAYEMS > 135000 but 5-day SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of such periods.
